name: Pushup RPG
tagline: Turns pushup sets into an RPG: log reps, gain XP, level up a character, keep a streak alive.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanic here is a counter with a progress bar wearing a fantasy hat, and that is not an insult, it is just the truth. XP curves, levels, streaks, and a daily quest list are the kind of logic an agent writes correctly on the first pass, and the whole thing fits in localStorage with no server. What you cannot one-shot is the part that actually makes people do pushups: art, sound, satisfying numbers, and copy that makes leveling up feel like something. If the app has leaderboards or friends nudging each other, that half does not come with you. Build it if you enjoy the building, because the DIY version will be honest about the fact that motivation was never a code problem.
coreLoopDIY: A local-first web app where you log pushup sets, earn XP on a tuned curve, level a character, track streaks, and see a history chart, all stored on your device.
requirements: A browser, and a device you will actually pick up mid workout
Optional: a static host if you want it on your phone as a PWA
whatYouLose: Character art, animations, and sound design that make a level up feel earned
Any social layer: leaderboards, guilds, friends who notice you skipped a day
Push notifications and reminders that work when the tab is closed
Balanced progression tuned against real user data instead of your first guess at an XP curve
Cross device sync, unless you bolt on a backend later
moatNotes: The defensible part is feel: pacing, art, and the exact sound when the bar fills. None of that is in the spec you write.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the gap between a working tracker and a thing you open every morning is entirely made of polish, and polish is the one deliverable you cannot brief into existence in a single session. People pay a few dollars once to skip the part where they build a motivation app and then lose motivation to use it. If there is a social or ranking component, that is also worth real money, since a leaderboard with one person on it is a spreadsheet.
notes: The logic is a weekend intro exercise; the dopamine engineering is the actual product.
prompt:
Build a local-first gamified pushup tracker as a single page web app. No accounts, no backend, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript, Tailwind for styling, Recharts for the history chart, zustand for state, all persisted to localStorage under one versioned key. No server, no database, no external API calls.

Core loop:
- A big primary button to log a set. Numeric input plus quick buttons for 5, 10, 20 reps.
- Each rep is 1 XP. Level thresholds follow a curve: level N requires floor(50 * N^1.5) cumulative XP. Show current level, XP into level, XP to next, and a progress bar that animates on gain.
- Streak logic: a day counts if total reps that day are at least the daily goal (default 20, editable in settings). Streak breaks after a missed calendar day. Track and display longest streak.
- Daily quests, generated deterministically from the date: e.g. "do 3 sets today", "hit 30 reps", "beat yesterday's total". Completing a quest grants bonus XP. Persist which quests were completed on which day.
- A character panel: a text based class and title that changes with level (tiers every 5 levels), plus three stats derived from history (total reps, best single set, consistency percent over the last 30 days).

Views: Today, History, Settings. History shows a 90 day bar chart of daily reps, a table of sets with timestamps, and per set delete. Settings has daily goal, character name, wipe all data with a confirm, and JSON export and import of the full save file.

Out of scope, do not build: leaderboards, friends, accounts, cloud sync, camera based rep counting, push notifications, sound effects, generated art.

Requirements: mobile first layout, thumb reachable log button, works fully offline, add a web app manifest and service worker so it installs to a phone home screen. Dark theme by default. No secrets needed, but if you add any config use .env and commit .env.example only.

Deliver a README with install, dev, build, and how the XP curve is tuned so it can be changed in one place.
